stem: A rooting-success KPI is defined as successful rooted units divided by eligible starting cuttings. There were 84 successful units from 100 eligible starts. What is the KPI?
choices: 16%, because 16 of the 100 eligible starts did not root.
100%, because the KPI should exclude unsuccessful cuttings once final viability is known.
84%, because the defined KPI uses 84 successful rooted units divided by 100 eligible starting cuttings.
The KPI cannot be calculated until the failed cuttings are assigned a cause.
rationale: The KPI definition already specifies both numerator and denominator. Eighty-four successful rooted units divided by 100 eligible starting cuttings equals 84%. Failed units remain part of the denominator unless a predefined eligibility rule excludes them independently of outcome. Changing the denominator after observing failures would bias the metric.
